title: On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem
core_idea: Defines the Turing machine — the minimal formal model of computation — and proves some problems are undecidable.
why_it_matters: Establishes the ceiling of what any intelligence, biological or artificial, can compute; every result below inherits this frame.

title: A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity
core_idea: Neurons as threshold logic units; networks of them compute any logical proposition.
why_it_matters: First proof that neural substrate ⇒ computation; the founding bridge between brain and mathematics.

title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
core_idea: Information = reduction of uncertainty (entropy); source coding and channel coding theorems; the bit.
why_it_matters: The vocabulary of every loss function (cross-entropy = Shannon information) and of compression-as-understanding. The single most-used equation in LLM training.

title: A Formal Theory of Inductive Inference
core_idea: Predict the future by Bayesian mixture over all computable hypotheses, weighted by 2^(−description length) (algorithmic probability).
why_it_matters: The mathematically ideal — though uncomputable — learner; modern sequence models are its practical approximation.

title: Three Approaches to the Quantitative Definition of Information
core_idea: Kolmogorov complexity: the length of the shortest program that outputs an object.
why_it_matters: "Understanding = compression" made precise; ties Occam's razor to computability.

title: Modeling by Shortest Data Description
core_idea: Minimum Description Length (MDL): prefer the model that compresses the data plus model code best.
why_it_matters: Practical model-selection principle uniting compression and generalization; ancestor of bits-per-byte evals.

title: On the Uniform Convergence of Relative Frequencies to Probabilities (VC theory)
core_idea: Generalization is controlled by the capacity (VC dimension) of the hypothesis class, not just sample count.
why_it_matters: Classical generalization theory — and the benchmark modern deep learning spectacularly violated (see Zhang 2017), forcing new theory.

title: Simplified Neuron Model as a Principal Component Analyzer
core_idea: A single neuron with Hebbian plasticity plus normalization converges to the first principal component of its input.
why_it_matters: Local, biologically plausible rules can compute global statistics — dimensionality reduction for free.

title: Neural Networks and Physical Systems with Emergent Collective Computational Abilities
core_idea: Recurrent binary networks as energy minima = content-addressable memory; physics (spin glasses) applied to neural systems.
why_it_matters: Founded the statistical-mechanics view of neural networks; modern "attention as associative memory" results trace here (Nobel Prize 2024, shared with Hinton).

title: A Theory of the Learnable
core_idea: PAC learning: learnable = efficiently learnable to arbitrary accuracy with high probability.
why_it_matters: Put learning itself on computational footing — learning has complexity classes like computation does.

title: A Learning Algorithm for Boltzmann Machines
authors: David Ackley, Geoffrey Hinton, Terrence Sejnowski
core_idea: Stochastic energy-based networks trained by contrasting data and model statistics.
why_it_matters: First usable learning rule for hidden-unit networks; ancestor of contrastive divergence, wake-sleep, and modern self-supervised losses.

title: Learning Representations by Back-Propagating Errors
authors: David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton, Ronald Williams
core_idea: Compute gradients of error through layers via the chain rule, making internal representations trainable.
why_it_matters: The learning algorithm of the entire deep learning era; still how every LLM trains.

title: The Space of Interactions in Neural Network Models (statistical mechanics of learning)
core_idea: Compute the volume of parameter space consistent with a training set — capacity thresholds and phase transitions in learning.
why_it_matters: Learning has thermodynamic phase transitions; this lens predicts grokking-like phenomena decades early.

title: Multilayer Feedforward Networks Are Universal Approximators
authors: Kurt Hornik, Maxwell Stinchcombe, Halbert White
core_idea: One hidden layer with enough units approximates any continuous function (independently: Cybenko 1989).
why_it_matters: Guarantees representational sufficiency — but says nothing about depth efficiency or learnability (see Poole 2017).

title: An Information-Maximization Approach to Blind Separation and Blind Deconvolution
core_idea: Maximize output entropy (InfoMax) and the network discovers independent sources — without labels.
why_it_matters: Information-theoretic self-supervision works; direct ancestor of contrastive and predictive self-supervised learning.

title: The Lack of A Priori Distinctions Between Learning Algorithms (No Free Lunch)
core_idea: Averaged over all possible problems, no learner beats random guessing.
why_it_matters: Generalization must come from inductive bias matched to the world's structure — explains why architecture and priors matter.

title: Collective Dynamics of 'Small-World' Networks
core_idea: Networks interpolating regular/random achieve high clustering with short path lengths (small-world).
why_it_matters: The architecture of brains, and increasingly of ML systems (MoE routing, agent swarms); a recurring mathematical pattern.

title: Emergence of Scaling in Random Networks
core_idea: Growth + preferential attachment produces power-law degree distributions (scale-free networks).
why_it_matters: Power laws appear in language (Zipf), brains, and model scaling — one generating mechanism, many systems.

title: Self-Organized Criticality: An Explanation of 1/f Noise
authors: Per Bak, Chao Tang, Kurt Wiesenfeld
core_idea: Driven dissipative systems self-tune to a critical point between order and chaos, producing scale-invariant avalanches.
why_it_matters: Candidate explanation for brain criticality (domain 04) and for why edge-of-chaos dynamics keep recurring in learning systems.

title: The Information Bottleneck Method
authors: Naftali Tishby, Fernando Pereira, William Bialek
core_idea: Optimal representations maximally compress X about irrelevant detail while preserving information about relevance variable Y; formally rate-distortion with a relevance constraint.
why_it_matters: The leading formal account of what a "good representation" is; frames deep learning as progressive information compression.

title: An Exact Mapping Between the Variational Renormalization Group and Deep Learning
core_idea: Stacked restricted Boltzmann machines perform the variational renormalization group exactly.
why_it_matters: Physics' tool for scale-dependent structure (RG) ≈ deep learning's stacked abstraction; concrete support for "deep = multi-scale".

title: Deep Learning and the Information Bottleneck Principle
core_idea: Deep networks should first fit (memorize) then compress representations — phases observed via mutual-information probes.
why_it_matters: Predicted a two-phase training dynamic later echoing in grokking (F10).

title: Group Equivariant Convolutional Networks
core_idea: Build symmetry (translation, rotation equivariance) into architecture rather than learning it from data.
why_it_matters: Symmetry is the strongest inductive bias physics knows; equivariant nets show architectural priors can replace data volume.

title: Exponential Expressivity in Deep Neural Networks through Transient Chaos
authors: Ben Poole, Surya Ganguli, Maithra Raghu (with "On the Expressivity of Deep Neural Networks", Raghu et al. 2017)
core_idea: Depth yields exponential gains in expressivity for representing compositional functions, beyond what width can buy.
why_it_matters: Why we stack layers instead of widening flat ones; why hierarchies (brains included) are deep.

title: Understanding Deep Learning Requires Rethinking Generalization
authors: Chiyuan Zhang, Samy Bengio, Moritz Hardt, Benjamin Recht, Oriol Vinyals
core_idea: Deep nets can fit random labels perfectly, so generalization cannot follow from classical capacity control alone.
why_it_matters: Broke VC-style theory of deep learning; opened implicit-regularization and double-descent research lines.

title: Opening the Black Box of Deep Neural Networks via Information
core_idea: Empirically observes the fit-then-compress information phases during SGD training.
why_it_matters: Made information-plane analysis famous — and triggered the field's sharpest theory debate.

title: On the Information Bottleneck Theory of Deep Learning
core_idea: Compression phases largely vanish with ReLU/unbounded activations and realistic datasets; IB theory is not the mechanism.
why_it_matters: The decisive rebuttal — science working; the field now treats IB as a design principle, not a law.

title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
authors: Arthur Jacot, Franck Gabriel, Clément Hongler
core_idea: In the infinite-width limit, training a network equals kernel regression with a fixed kernel (NTK).
why_it_matters: Makes one training regime exactly solvable — and marks its boundary: NTK-lazy networks do NOT learn features.

title: On Lazy Training in Differentiable Programming
authors: Lénaïc Chizat, Edouard Oyallon, Francis Bach
core_idea: Two regimes: lazy (kernel-like, features fixed) vs rich (feature learning); initialization scale selects the regime.
why_it_matters: Feature learning — the rich regime — is what makes deep learning work; connects to grokking transitions.

title: Reconciling Modern Machine-Learning Practice and the Classical Bias–Variance Trade-Off
authors: Mikhail Belkin, Daniel Hsu, Siyuan Ma, Soumik Mandal
core_idea: Double descent: test error descends, peaks at the interpolation threshold, then descends again as overparameterization grows.
why_it_matters: The modern generalization curve; explains why billion-parameter models on "small" data behave well.

title: Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt
core_idea: Double descent is ubiquitous across model size, data size, and training time in modern deep learning.
why_it_matters: Practical warning: more parameters/data can hurt before they help; scale results have regime boundaries.

title: Visualizing the Loss Landscape of Neural Nets
authors: Hao Li, Zheng Xu, Gavin Taylor, Christoph Studer, Tom Goldstein
core_idea: Filter-normalized visualization shows residual nets have trainable convex-ish valleys; without skip connections landscapes are chaotic.
why_it_matters: Explains why residual connections (ResNet, transformer) made depth trainable — geometry, not just gradients.

title: Neural Collapse: An Analysis of the Modes of Neural Network Classifiers
authors: Vardan Papyan, X. Y. Han, David Donoho
core_idea: At training's end, last-layer features collapse to class means arranged as a simplex ETF — a sharp geometric universal.
why_it_matters: 2025 work unifies grokking and information bottleneck via neural collapse; a concrete geometry of "converged" learning.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
core_idea: Loss follows smooth power laws in parameters, data, and compute, across 6+ orders of magnitude.
why_it_matters: Made scaling a predictive engineering discipline: you can read next year's loss off this year's curves.

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)
core_idea: For fixed compute, parameters and tokens should scale equally (~20 tokens/parameter) — most 2021-era models were badly undertrained.
why_it_matters: The recipe behind every efficient model since (LLaMA etc.); GPT-3-sized results from 4× smaller models.

title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
core_idea: Networks memorize quickly but suddenly generalize long after overfitting, when trained past the point of zero training loss.
why_it_matters: Separates memorization from understanding in time; a lab model of "aha moment" learning.

title: Towards Understanding Grokking: An Effective Theory of Representation Learning
authors: Ziming Liu, Ouail Kitouni, Mike Nolte, Eric Michaud, Max Tegmark, Mike Williams
core_idea: Grokking = delayed generalization explained by a effective-theory of representation learning dynamics.
why_it_matters: First mechanistic theory; predicts when grokking happens from dataset properties.

title: Omnigrok: Grokking Beyond Algorithmic Data
authors: Ziming Liu, Eric Michaud, Max Tegmark
core_idea: Grokking occurs on image datasets too; driven by weight-norm scale — "LU mechanism": memorize large-norm, generalize small-norm.
why_it_matters: Grokking is general, and controllable via weight decay — a knob for generalization.

title: Progress Measures for Grokking via Mechanistic Interpretability
authors: Neel Nanda, Lawrence Chan, Tom Lieberum, Jess Smith, Jacob Steinhardt
core_idea: Reverse-engineers a grokking network: it transitions from memorization to a generalizing Fourier/multiplication circuit; restricted-set "pre-grokking" progress measures predict the transition.
why_it_matters: The cleanest causal story of emergent generalization inside a network; mechanistic interpretability's flagship result.

title: Grokking as the Transition from Lazy to Rich Training Dynamics
authors: Kaifeng Lyu, Zhiyuan Li, et al. (ICLR 2024)
core_idea: Networks grok when they escape the lazy kernel regime into rich feature learning late in training.
why_it_matters: Unifies grokking with the NTK/lazy-rich framework — one theory for both phenomena.

title: Grokking Explained: A Statistical Phenomenon
core_idea: Grokking reinterpreted as a distribution shift between training and test data rather than an optimization mystery.
why_it_matters: The 2025 theory pivot: grokking may be statistical, not dynamical — with direct implications for what "generalization" means for LLM evals.

title: A Survey on Grokking
core_idea: Systematizes all grokking explanations: norm-based, circuit-formation, statistical, physics-based (glass relaxation).
why_it_matters: Entry point to the whole grokking literature; includes 2025 evidence of grokking during 7B-parameter pretraining (OLMoE).

title: Superposition Yields Robust Neural Scaling
core_idea: Neural scaling laws arise mechanistically from superposition — networks storing more features than neurons in interference-prone ways.
why_it_matters: First mechanistic account of WHY scaling laws exist, linking interpretability (domain 03) with scaling theory.

title: A Limit Theory of Foundation Models
core_idea: A rigorous mathematical limit theory for foundation models, extending scaling-law analysis to data quality and training strategies.
why_it_matters: Theoretical frontier (as of 2026): scaling laws are becoming a full limit theory rather than curve fits.

title: Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models
core_idea: Repeating data helps up to ~4 epochs, then returns diminish sharply; unique tokens dominate value.
why_it_matters: The data side of scaling laws — governs planning when internet text runs out; motivates synthetic data and RL data loops.

title: Universal Artificial Intelligence / AIXI
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.0801 (Legg & Hutter, "Universal Intelligence: A Definition of Machine Intelligence", 2007)
core_idea: Intelligence = expected reward maximization over all computable environments weighted by algorithmic probability (AIXI); uncomputable but defines the optimum.
why_it_matters: The formal reference point every practical intelligence (including LLMs) is measured against; Legg-Hutter gives the field's cleanest intelligence definition.

title: On the Measure of Intelligence
core_idea: Intelligence = skill-acquisition efficiency over novel tasks, not skill itself; introduces the ARC benchmark built on core knowledge priors.
why_it_matters: Corrects the benchmark-culture error (skill ≠ intelligence); ARC-AGI remains the reference test for generalization (domain 05).
